project.name: retro-board
project.title: Retro Board
project.idea: A retrospective board for small engineering teams. A facilitator creates a board per sprint, teammates add anonymous cards into Start / Stop / Continue columns, then everyone votes and the team leaves with three agreed actions. Today teams do this in a shared doc that nobody can vote on and that loses its history.

primitives.title: Product brief
primitives.why: An agent fills every ambiguity silently. A written brief is the cheapest place to remove ambiguity.

primitives.title: Non-goals and scope discipline
primitives.why: Scope creep is the default failure mode of generated code; explicit non-goals are the brake.

primitives.title: Ubiquitous language and DDD basics
primitives.why: Shared vocabulary is the highest-leverage defence against plausible-but-wrong generated code.

primitives.title: Test-driven loop
primitives.why: A failing test is the only instruction an agent cannot misinterpret.

primitives.title: Acceptance criteria and traceability anchors
primitives.why: Requirement-to-test anchors are the mechanism that closes the enforcement gap.

primitives.title: Agent handoff packet
primitives.why: The spec is useless if the agent that receives it cannot find the entry point.

primitives.title: Aggregates and invariants
primitives.why: Invariants are the properties mutation and property-based tests verify.

primitives.title: Architecture style selection
primitives.why: Default to a modular monolith; distributed complexity must be justified, not inherited.

primitives.title: Secrets and supply chain hygiene
primitives.why: Leaked keys and unpinned dependencies are the two cheapest attacks on a new product.

primitives.title: CI gates from the first commit
primitives.why: A gate that does not run in CI is a suggestion.

primitives.title: User journeys as testable slices
primitives.why: Journeys turn a paragraph of intent into testable slices.

primitives.title: Bounded contexts and module seams
primitives.why: Context boundaries decide module seams before any file is generated.

primitives.title: Contract before implementation
primitives.why: A contract written before implementation is the only interface an agent cannot improvise.

primitives.title: Schema and forward-only migrations
primitives.why: Schemas outlive code. Forward-only migrations keep the data recoverable.

primitives.title: Test budget and suite shape
primitives.why: Test suite shape must match risk: heavy on domain rules, thin on frameworks.

primitives.title: Authorization model, deny by default
primitives.why: Authorization bugs are invisible in happy-path demos and catastrophic in production.
primitives.when: (traits includes "auth" OR risks.multiTenant eq true OR traits includes "admin")

primitives.title: OWASP ASVS baseline
primitives.why: OWASP ASVS gives a numbered baseline where there is a network surface or a credential; a local tool inherits supply-chain hygiene instead.
primitives.when: tier gte 1 AND (kind in ["web-app","api","mobile"] OR risks.publicFacing eq true OR traits includes "auth")

primitives.title: Design tokens and UI consistency
primitives.why: One token source prevents the brownish-green drift typical of generated UIs.

primitives.title: Accessibility baseline
primitives.why: Keyboard and screen-reader support is not retrofittable for free.

primitives.title: UI state model: loading, empty, error, success
primitives.why: Agents implement the happy path; loading, empty and error states are where products feel broken.

primitives.title: Automated review protocol
primitives.why: Self-review is theatre when the reviewer shares the author's blind spots.

primitives.title: Ports and adapters (hexagonal)
primitives.why: Keeping the domain free of framework and vendor code is what makes later replacement cheap.

requirements.title: Runnable from a clean clone
requirements.statement: The application shall start, run its tests and name every missing environment variable from a clean clone using only the commands in the README.
requirements.failurePath: A missing environment variable produces a single actionable error naming the variable, not a stack trace deep in a startup path.

acceptance.text: Given a fresh clone and an empty environment file, when the documented setup command runs, then it either succeeds or lists every missing required variable by name.

requirements.title: The primary journey works end to end
requirements.statement: The application shall carry one record through the journey in the product brief from first step to last, through the documented interface, and leave the promised outcome readable on a second visit.
requirements.failurePath: If any step of the journey fails, the user is left in a state they can retry from, with no partially written data and an explanation that names what failed.

acceptance.text: Given a new user and empty storage, when they complete the primary journey using only the documented interface, then the outcome named in the brief exists and is readable on a second visit.
Given the same journey, when a dependency it relies on is unavailable, then the user sees an actionable message and no partial record is created.

requirements.title: Explicit non-goals
requirements.statement: The product brief shall name at least three capabilities this version deliberately does not provide, with no partially built version of them anywhere in the codebase.
requirements.failurePath: Out-of-scope work arrives as a failing review comment referencing a non-goal, rather than as silent extra code.

acceptance.text: Given the brief, when a reviewer reads the change, then every capability in the diff maps to an in-scope requirement or is rejected.

requirements.title: Durable state with forward-only migrations
requirements.statement: When the schema of stored state changes, the application shall apply a forward-only migration that runs against a non-empty database without losing data.
requirements.failurePath: A migration that fails halfway leaves the database in a known state, and the documented restore step returns it to the pre-migration snapshot.

acceptance.text: Given a database at the previous schema version with representative rows, when the migration runs, then all rows remain readable and no column required by the new code is null.
Given the same database, when the migration is re-run, then it is a no-op rather than an error.

requirements.title: Authentication with explicit session lifecycle
requirements.statement: While a session is open, the application shall accept it only after verifying it server-side, and expire or revoke it on the documented triggers.
requirements.failurePath: An expired or revoked session receives an unauthenticated response and performs no state change.

acceptance.text: Given valid credentials, when the user signs in, then a session is issued and the identifier is not placed in a URL.
Given a revoked session, when any protected endpoint is called, then the response is 401 and no data is written.
Given a sign-out-everywhere request, when any previously issued session is used, then all are rejected except the current one.

requirements.title: Server-side authorization with deny-by-default
requirements.statement: When a request reads or changes data belonging to another subject, the application shall deny it unless a named role or policy grants that action on that object.
requirements.failurePath: A forbidden request returns 403 or 404 as documented, writes nothing, and emits an authorization-denied log line without leaking the resource's contents.

acceptance.text: Given a user without the required role, when the operation is attempted directly against the API, then it is refused even if the UI hides the control.
Given a resource owned by another subject, when it is requested by identifier, then the response does not reveal existence.

requirements.title: Accessible primary journey
requirements.statement: When the primary journey is run with a keyboard alone or with a screen reader, the interface shall complete every step with visible focus, labelled controls and no colour-only status.
requirements.failurePath: Validation errors are announced and focus moves to the first invalid field, rather than the form silently failing.

acceptance.text: Given the primary journey, when it is driven by keyboard only, then every control is reachable and the outcome is completed.
Given a form submission with an invalid field, when it fails, then an error message is programmatically associated with that field and announced.

requirements.title: Every screen has loading, empty, error and success states
requirements.statement: When a data-driven screen is empty, loading or has failed, the interface shall show that defined state and, when empty, name the next action.
requirements.failurePath: A failed request shows a retry affordance and preserves the user's input rather than discarding the form.

acceptance.text: Given a slow response, when the screen loads, then a loading state appears within 200ms and does not shift layout.
Given zero records, when the screen loads, then an empty state with a single next action is shown.
Given a server error, when the request fails, then an error state with a working retry is shown.

requirements.title: One design token source
requirements.statement: The interface shall take colour, spacing, typography and radius from one token source, with no component hard-coding a hex value, pixel spacing or font family.
requirements.failurePath: A component using a raw value fails the design-token fitness check in CI.

acceptance.text: Given the component directory, when the token check runs, then no raw colour or spacing literal is reported.

requirements.title: Errors are classified before they are rendered
requirements.statement: When an operation fails, the interface shall classify the failure as user-correctable, retryable or unexpected and apply that class's one presentation and logging rule.
requirements.failurePath: Unexpected errors never render internal messages, stack traces or identifiers to the user, and are logged with a correlation ID that is shown as a short support code.

acceptance.text: Given a forced internal failure, when it is displayed, then the user sees a generic message plus a support code and the server log contains the matching correlation ID.

requirements.title: Versioned machine-readable interface contract
requirements.statement: When an exposed or consumed interface changes, the application shall update the machine-readable contract in the repository before merge, in a form a breaking-change check can reject.
requirements.failurePath: An incompatible change fails the contract check and names the field and the consumer affected.

acceptance.text: Given the contract and the implementation, when the contract check runs, then they agree on paths, methods, status codes and error shape.
Given a removed response field, when the check runs, then it fails as a breaking change.

requirements.title: One error envelope and one identifier scheme
requirements.statement: The application shall return every error in one envelope carrying a stable machine code, a human message, a correlation ID and optional field details, with opaque identifiers instead of sequential ones.
requirements.failurePath: An unknown route and a failed validation return the same envelope shape with distinguishable machine codes.

acceptance.text: Given an invalid payload, when the response is inspected, then its shape matches the documented envelope and the machine code is stable across releases.

requirements.title: Abuse limits on public entry points
requirements.statement: When a public write or authentication endpoint is called, the application shall limit requests per identity and per IP and answer a refused request with a retry hint.
requirements.failurePath: Exceeding the limit returns 429 with a retry hint and performs no work; the limiter fails closed for authentication endpoints.

acceptance.text: Given N+1 requests within the window, when the last is made, then it is refused with 429 and no state change occurred.

requirements.title: The product's own rules are named and pinned
requirements.statement: The domain model shall state every product-specific invariant as a rule, each pinned by an automated test that fails when the rule is inverted.
requirements.failurePath: If a core rule is inverted by a refactor, a test fails and names the rule, rather than the change being discovered by a user or a reviewer.

acceptance.text: Given the invariants listed in the domain model, when the suite runs, then each invariant is covered by a test that fails if its rule is inverted.
Given an invariant added to the domain model, when it has no test, then the review checklist rejects the change.

gates.statement: The project starts from a clean clone with one documented command.

enforcement.proves: The README contains a fenced command block a new contributor can copy.
enforcement.doesNotProve: The README itself. This check only proves a command is written down; G0-SMOKE proves it works.

gates.statement: Lint or typecheck runs in CI on every pull request.

enforcement.proves: A CI workflow runs a lint or typecheck step on pull requests.
enforcement.doesNotProve: The workflow file. Add the same command to the README so a local run matches CI.

gates.statement: One happy-path smoke test exercises the primary user journey.

enforcement.proves: A smoke or end-to-end test file exists for the primary journey.
enforcement.doesNotProve: One end-to-end test, exercising the documented interface rather than the internals.

gates.statement: The full test suite runs in CI on every pull request and is required to merge.

enforcement.proves: A CI workflow runs the test command.
enforcement.doesNotProve: The workflow file, plus a branch protection rule that makes the job required. The rule is in the forge, not in the repository.

gates.statement: Every rule in the domain model has at least one automated test.

enforcement.proves: Every core requirement carries an @req anchor in a test file.
enforcement.doesNotProve: `spec-check.mjs` counts the anchors; this gate fails while a core requirement has none.

gates.statement: Every requirement marked automated maps to a named test through an @req anchor.

enforcement.proves: Every requirement marked automated has a test anchor.

gates.statement: README documents how to run, test and deploy, plus known limitations.

enforcement.proves: The README covers running, testing and deploying.
enforcement.doesNotProve: Three headings. A runbook with none of them is a README for the author.

gates.statement: No secret is committed; configuration comes from the environment and is validated at startup.

enforcement.proves: No credential-shaped string is committed, and a gitleaks config is present for the pre-commit hook.
enforcement.doesNotProve: The runner scans the working tree; gitleaks scans history. Both are needed: this file cannot see what was already committed and deleted.
